title: Artist Booking Agreement (Show/Event)
money_fields: Guaranteed fee, deposit, and balance due date | Percentage of door/ticket sales, if applicable, and how it's verified | Who covers travel/lodging
rights_grant_notes: Confirms this is a one-off (or short run) live performance service, not an ongoing exclusive booking relationship
control_fields: Set time and length | Merch selling rights at the venue and any commission the venue takes | Recording/broadcast rights for the performance — does the artist retain rights to any recording of the show?
intake_questions: What's the date, venue, fee, and payment structure (flat guarantee vs. door split)? | What deposit is required and when is the balance due? | Does the promoter want to record or livestream the show? If so, on what terms? | What are the merch terms at this show?
risk_1_text: no deposit required — increases risk of a no-pay cancellation.
risk_2_text: broad recording/broadcast rights grant to the venue/promoter with no artist approval or compensation for later use.

title: Artist / Label Recording Agreement
money_fields: Advance amount and recoupment structure | Royalty rate (% of net receipts) and how it's calculated | Recording fund / budget and whether unspent funds go to the artist | Whether costs (video, marketing, tour support) are recoupable or cross-collateralized against other income
rights_grant_notes: Who owns the masters — Label (traditional deal), Artist with a license to Label (artist-friendly/distribution deal), or a joint venture | Territory and format (all media now known or later devised is broad — flag it) | Whether rights are exclusive to this label or the artist can also self-release other work
control_fields: Album/song delivery commitment (how many records, minimum length/quality standard) | Creative control over artwork, singles, mixing/mastering, release timing | Options: does the label have the right to pick up further albums, and on what terms? | Term and what happens if the label doesn't release the record within X months (reversion)
intake_questions: Does the artist want to keep master ownership (distribution-style deal) or is a traditional ownership transfer acceptable given the advance/support offered? | What advance, if any, is on the table, and what specifically does it need to cover? | How many albums/songs is this deal for, and is there an option for more? | What happens if the label doesn't release the music — is there a release deadline with reversion rights? | What creative approvals does the artist want to keep (single choice, artwork, video treatment)?
risk_1_text: perpetual or 'life of copyright' master ownership transfer with no reversion.
risk_2_text: cross-collateralization across unrelated projects (video costs recouped from touring, etc.).
risk_3_text: vague 'all rights in all media now known or hereafter devised, throughout the universe' language — push for defined scope.
risk_4_text: open-ended multi-album options with no minimum advance guaranteed for later albums.

title: Artist Management Agreement
money_fields: Commission rate (typically 15-20% of gross income) | What income is commissionable (recording, publishing, touring, merch, brand deals, sync) | What is excluded (e.g., pre-existing deals, songwriting-only income if a separate publisher exists) | Commission on income earned after termination (post-term/sunset commission) and for how long
rights_grant_notes: Manager is NOT granted ownership of masters or compositions — management is a service, not an ownership stake | Power of attorney scope, if any — should be narrow (signing on artist's behalf only for specifically listed acts)
control_fields: Exclusivity: is the Manager the artist's only manager, or only for certain territories/activities? | Term length and whether there are renewal options tied to performance benchmarks | Termination triggers: for cause (breach, fraud, inactivity) and for convenience (notice period) | Key-person clause if signing with a management company, not an individual
intake_questions: Is this a new relationship or formalizing an existing informal one? (If informal, note the actual start date — commission disputes often hinge on this.) | What commission rate did they agree on verbally, if any? | Is the manager an individual or does the artist need to contract with their company? | Does the artist already have a separate publisher, booking agent, or label? (affects what's commissionable and avoids double-commissioning) | How long should the initial term run, and should renewal depend on the manager hitting specific milestones (e.g., securing a certain amount of income)?
risk_1_text: commission on ALL income for life, or with no sunset after termination.
risk_2_text: manager also acting as booking agent, label, or publisher without disclosure — commission stacking.
risk_3_text: automatic renewal options with no artist opt-out or performance trigger.
risk_4_text: broad power of attorney allowing the manager to sign contracts or spend money without artist sign-off.

title: Booking / Talent Agent Agreement
money_fields: Commission rate on gross performance fees (industry norm ~10-20%) | Who pays deposit/travel/rider costs and whether they're deducted before or after commission | Minimum guarantee or fee floor the agent must secure, if any
rights_grant_notes: Agent is granted the right to solicit and negotiate performance offers on artist's behalf — not ownership of anything
control_fields: Exclusive vs. non-exclusive, and for which territory (city/region/country/worldwide) | Whether the artist must run other offers through the agent or can self-book certain shows | Term and notice period to terminate | Whether the agent needs artist sign-off before accepting an offer, or has standing authority up to a certain fee
intake_questions: What territory does this agent actually work — local, regional, national, international? | Should the artist be able to book shows themselves without commission, or is everything exclusive? | What's the agreed commission percentage, and is it before or after travel/production costs? | Is there a minimum number of shows/income the agent must deliver to keep the exclusive?
risk_1_text: worldwide exclusivity when the agent only actually has relationships in one region.
risk_2_text: no minimum activity requirement — agent can sit on exclusive rights without booking anything.
risk_3_text: agent given authority to accept offers and bind the artist without prior approval.

title: Brand Sponsorship Agreement
money_fields: Sponsorship fee structure and payment schedule | Performance bonuses/milestones, if any (streams, event attendance, social metrics)
rights_grant_notes: What exactly is licensed — name, likeness, music, social content — and for what use (events, advertising, product packaging) | Term length and renewal terms
control_fields: Category exclusivity (artist can't endorse a competing brand) | Creative approval over how the brand uses the artist's name/image | Morals/reputation clause — mutual, not one-sided
intake_questions: What's the campaign scope — single activation, ongoing partnership, tour sponsorship? | What's the fee and payment schedule, and are there performance bonuses? | What exclusivity is the brand asking for, and does it conflict with any existing deals? | Does the artist want a morals clause to be mutual (either side can exit for cause)?
risk_1_text: one-sided morals clause that lets the brand terminate for any reputational issue, with no equivalent protection for the artist if the brand does something damaging.
risk_2_text: broad category exclusivity with no carve-out for the artist's existing deals.

title: Copyright License Agreement (Mechanical/Publisher License)
money_fields: Royalty rate per record/stream/unit sold | Accounting frequency and cure period if payments are late
rights_grant_notes: Non-exclusive vs. exclusive license, and to which specific recording/artist/label — should be narrowly scoped, not blanket rights to the composition
control_fields: What happens if the licensee stops paying — cancellation rights, and whether that ends only the license or also the underlying obligations
intake_questions: What specific recording, artist, and label is this license limited to? | What per-unit royalty rate was agreed? | How often should royalty statements be sent?
risk_1_text: license not limited to a specific artist/recording/label — could be read as broader than intended.
risk_2_text: built-in cancellation-on-nonpayment clause protects the publisher.

title: DJ Booking Agreement
money_fields: Total fee, deposit amount and due date, balance due date (usually night of show) | Travel, lodging, and hospitality rider costs — who pays
rights_grant_notes: Confirms this is a performance service, not a transfer of any recording or composition rights
control_fields: Set length and time slot | Exclusivity radius (can the DJ play another show nearby before/after this date?) | Cancellation policy for both sides and refund of deposit
intake_questions: What's the date, venue, and set length/time slot? | What's the total fee, deposit amount, and when is the balance due? | Is there a radius clause restricting other local shows around this date? | What happens if either side needs to cancel — refund policy and notice period?
risk_1_text: no cancellation/force majeure clause — DJ has no protection if the venue cancels last-minute.
risk_2_text: deposit non-specified — always get a deposit for club/private bookings.

title: Exclusive Beat License Agreement
money_fields: Purchase price and payment schedule (deposit vs. full payment) | Whether a separate publishing split applies on top of the purchase price
rights_grant_notes: Clarify up front: is this an exclusive LICENSE (producer keeps underlying copyright, artist can't resell the beat itself) or a full BUYOUT (producer assigns copyright entirely)? These are priced very differently and the template defaults to license unless Section 4(c) is activated. | Confirm whether the beat is being removed from beat-store/marketplace listings once paid — this is what 'exclusive' actually means operationally, not just legally
control_fields: Reversion window if the artist never releases anything using the beat | Producer credit requirement and exact tag wording
intake_questions: Is this a full buyout (producer keeps nothing) or an exclusive license (producer keeps underlying ownership but can't sell to anyone else)? | What's the purchase price, and is it paid upfront or as a deposit + balance on delivery? | What publishing percentage does the producer keep on the finished song? | Is there a deadline by which the artist needs to release something, after which the producer can take the beat back?
risk_1_text: are they aware they're giving up the right to sell this beat to anyone else, permanently, for this price? Producers sometimes under-price exclusives without registering what they're giving up.
risk_2_text: no reversion clause — if the artist never uses the beat, the producer is locked out of ever selling it again with no time limit.
risk_3_text: publishing split percentage left blank — this is a real revenue stream, not boilerplate; don't let it default silently.

title: Independent Contractor Agreement (General Services)
money_fields: Flat fee, retainer, or per-session rate | Payment schedule and reimbursable-expense pre-approval
rights_grant_notes: This is the catch-all template — use it for PR, marketing, social media management, or single-date session work that doesn't have its own dedicated template. The single most important decision is Section 5: work-for-hire (client owns everything) vs. licensed use (contractor keeps ownership, client gets a license).
control_fields: Deliverables, deadlines, and included revision rounds | Term and notice period to terminate | Whether the contractor is free to work with other clients (should be yes, by default, unless real exclusivity is negotiated and paid for)
intake_questions: What specific services, deliverables, and deadlines are involved? | What's the fee structure — flat fee, retainer, or per-session? | Should the deliverables be a full work-for-hire buyout, or does the contractor keep ownership and license use to the client? | Is any exclusivity actually intended, or is the contractor free to work with others?
risk_1_text: — a contractor should never end up in a work-for-hire arrangement by default without understanding they're giving up all future rights to what they create.
risk_2_text: independent contractor status claimed but the actual working relationship looks like employment (set hours, exclusive availability, day-to-day supervision) — this can create real legal risk for the hiring party depending on jurisdiction; flag it rather than silently drafting around it.

title: Influencer / Content Creator Agreement
money_fields: Flat fee vs. performance-based (affiliate/commission) compensation | Payment schedule tied to deliverables
rights_grant_notes: What usage rights does the brand get to the content — organic posting only, or paid ad usage ('whitelisting'), and for how long? | Does the brand own the content, or just license it?
control_fields: Number and type of deliverables (posts, stories, videos) and approval/revision process | Required FTC disclosure language (#ad, #sponsored) | Category exclusivity (can't promote a competing brand for X period)
intake_questions: What deliverables are expected (# of posts, platform, format) and by when? | Is the brand asking to run the content as paid ads ('whitelisting')? If so, that needs separate, time-limited compensation. | Is there a category exclusivity requirement, and for how long? | What's the payment structure — flat fee, commission, or both?
risk_1_text: perpetual, unlimited paid-ad usage rights to the creator's likeness/content for a one-time flat fee — this is usually worth significantly more and should be priced separately or time-limited.
risk_2_text: no FTC disclosure requirement written into the contract — legal risk for the creator, not just the brand.
risk_3_text: broad exclusivity/non-compete with no time limit.

title: Joint Venture Publishing Agreement
money_fields: Cash and property contributed by each partner | Percentage of net profit/loss per partner
rights_grant_notes: This creates a business entity/relationship, not a simple license — treat as high-stakes and recommend attorney/accountant review by default given ongoing shared liability
control_fields: How new partners can be admitted (should require unanimous consent) | What happens on a partner's death, bankruptcy, or exit — does the JV continue? | Decision-making process for the JV's business
intake_questions: Who are all the partners, and what is each contributing (cash, catalog, distribution, services)? | What percentage of profit/loss does each partner receive? | Has the user considered forming an actual LLC for liability protection instead of an informal joint venture? (often the better artist-protective default — see the LLC Operating Agreement template)
risk_1_text: Joint ventures create ongoing shared liability and profit obligations — this is not a one-off contract, it's a business relationship.
risk_2_text: no clear exit/buyout mechanism if one partner wants out or the relationship breaks down.

title: LLC Operating Agreement (Music Venture)
money_fields: Capital contributions per member | Distribution schedule and priority (return of capital before profit split, etc.)
rights_grant_notes: Defines company-level ownership of the business itself (and by extension, any IP the LLC holds), separate from any individual artist's personal masters/publishing — clarify what assets actually sit inside the LLC
control_fields: Voting rights and what requires unanimous vs. majority approval | Buy-sell provisions: what happens if a member wants to leave, dies, or wants to sell their stake | Admission of new members
intake_questions: How many members, and what percentage does each hold? | Is this member-managed (all members vote on decisions) or manager-managed (one or a few run day-to-day)? | What happens if a member wants to exit, stops contributing, or the members disagree on a major decision? | What state will the LLC be formed in? (This determines filing requirements outside this document — recommend confirming with a local attorney or formation service.)
risk_1_text: for LLC formation documents — state-specific filing requirements and tax elections matter and are outside this skill's scope.
risk_2_text: no buy-sell/exit provision — can trap members in a business relationship with no clean way out.

title: Merchandise License Agreement
money_fields: Royalty rate on net sales (industry range roughly 8-15%) | Advance, if any, and whether it's recoupable against royalties
rights_grant_notes: Confirms the artist/band keeps ownership of their name/logo/trademarks — this is a license to manufacture and sell, not a transfer of the brand itself
control_fields: Product categories covered (don't grant broader categories than intended) | Approval rights over samples before production | Sell-off period after termination so the licensee isn't stuck with unsellable inventory, but also isn't selling forever
intake_questions: What product categories are covered (apparel, vinyl, posters, accessories)? | Exclusive or non-exclusive, and in what territory? | What royalty rate, and is there an advance? | Does the artist want sample-approval rights before products go into production?
risk_1_text: no minimum sales/good-faith-efforts requirement on an exclusive license — licensee can sit on the rights without actually selling anything.
risk_2_text: no sell-off period defined for after termination — creates disputes about existing inventory.
risk_3_text: built-in quality-control/sample-approval clause protects brand integrity — keep this even if the user is eager to move fast.

title: Music Distribution Agreement
money_fields: Distributor's fee/revenue share percentage | Accounting frequency
rights_grant_notes: Confirms the artist keeps ownership of masters and compositions — distribution is a service, not a rights transfer, unless the user is dealing with a distributor unusually asking for more
control_fields: Exclusive vs. non-exclusive distribution rights | Takedown rights and how fast the artist can pull a release | Whether this covers one release or an ongoing catalog relationship
intake_questions: Is this for one release or an ongoing relationship covering future releases too? | What's the distributor's fee/revenue share, and how often will they pay out? | Does the artist want the ability to pull the release down quickly if needed?
risk_1_text: a 'distributor' asking for ownership of masters or an equity stake in the recordings — that's no longer a distribution deal, it's a label deal, and should be evaluated as one (see Artist/Label Recording Agreement).
risk_2_text: no defined accounting schedule — distributors should report and pay on a predictable cycle.

title: NDA / Non-Circumvention Agreement
money_fields: Typically no payment terms — this is a protective document, not a deal itself
rights_grant_notes: Confirms this grants NO license or ownership of anything — it only protects information and relationships while a deal is being discussed
control_fields: Duration of confidentiality (2-3 years is typical) and non-circumvention (1-2 years) | Whether this is mutual (both sides protected) or should be one-directional
intake_questions: What's actually being protected — an unreleased song, a business plan, deal terms, a contact introduction? | Is information flowing both ways (mutual) or mostly one direction (should be unilateral instead)? | Is there a specific introduction (a contact, a potential deal) that needs non-circumvention protection, and for how long?
risk_1_text: signing this before sharing an unreleased track, deal terms, or a business introduction is a low-cost, high-value habit — encourage it even for casual-seeming conversations.
risk_2_text: if only one party is actually disclosing sensitive information, consider whether a one-way (unilateral) version is more appropriate than mutual — ask which direction the sensitive info is flowing.

title: Non-Exclusive Beat License Agreement
money_fields: License fee (typically the lowest tier a producer sells)
rights_grant_notes: This is a LICENSE, not ownership — the producer can and will sell the same beat to other artists. Make sure the user understands that before they build a whole campaign around a beat they don't have exclusive rights to.
control_fields: Usage caps (stream/download limits, no broadcast/sync/paid ads without upgrading) | Upgrade path to exclusive if the song starts to take off
intake_questions: What's the license fee, and what usage tier (streams, video use, no broadcast) is being purchased? | Does the artist plan to push this song commercially at scale? If so, discuss upgrading to exclusive before finalizing a release plan.
risk_1_text: if the artist's song starts getting real traction, this license's usage caps can become a real problem (e.g., it wasn't licensed for broadcast or paid ads). Recommend upgrading to an exclusive license before the song is pushed commercially at scale.
risk_2_text: clear, low-cost way to test a beat before committing to an exclusive purchase — appropriate default for early-stage work.

title: Producer / Composer Agreement
money_fields: Flat fee vs. royalty points (or both) | Payment schedule (deposit, on-delivery, on-release) | Whether points are paid on net or gross, and from what revenue streams (streaming, sync, physical)
rights_grant_notes: Is this work-for-hire (commissioning party owns everything) or does the producer/composer retain a royalty/points interest and credit? | Sample/loop clearance responsibility — who warrants the material is clean
control_fields: Number of revisions/rounds included in the fee before extra charges apply | Delivery format and deadline | Credit requirements (liner notes, streaming metadata, video credits)
intake_questions: Is this a flat-fee work-for-hire, or does the producer/composer keep a royalty/points interest? | What's the fee, and what payment milestones trigger payment? | How many revision rounds are included before additional charges apply? | What credit does the producer/composer receive, and where (streaming, liner notes, video)?
risk_1_text: 'full buyout, no further compensation' language when the producer expected points — clarify before signing.
risk_2_text: no defined revision limit, opening the door to unlimited free rework.
risk_3_text: producer required to warrant sample clearance without being told what samples were used.

title: Producer Royalties Agreement
money_fields: Royalty rate (points), typically 2-5% of net receipts for a non-featured producer | Whether points are 'all-in' (paid from the artist's royalty) or paid on top by the label | Recoupment: are producer points subject to recoupment of the artist's advance, or paid from first dollar?
rights_grant_notes: Confirms this is a royalty arrangement, not ownership of the master
control_fields: Accounting frequency (quarterly/semi-annual) and statement/audit rights | Credit requirements | What happens to points if the track is remixed, re-released, or used in a compilation
intake_questions: What point rate did the producer and artist/label agree to? | Are the points 'all-in' (from the artist's share) or paid separately by the label? | How often will royalty statements be sent, and does the producer want audit rights?
risk_1_text: no defined accounting schedule or audit right — producer has no way to verify they're being paid correctly.
risk_2_text: points defined as 'all-in' without the producer understanding that means splitting the artist's own royalty, not extra money from the label.

title: Production Agreement (Producer / Production Company)
money_fields: Recording budget and who fronts it | Recoupment of production costs from future deals | Producer's percentage of any deal secured (development/shopping fee)
rights_grant_notes: Does the production company own the masters during development, with a plan to shop to labels, or is this artist-owned with a paid producer? | What happens to ownership if the production company secures a label deal — do they keep a piece as a production/JV deal?
control_fields: Exclusivity during the development term | Term length and what happens if no deal is secured | Approval rights over which labels/deals the artist can accept
intake_questions: Is the goal to get shopped to a label, self-release, or both? | Who is funding the recording — the production company, the artist, or split? | If a label deal is secured, what percentage or role does the production company keep? | What's the outside date — if no deal happens by [date], do all rights revert to the artist?
risk_1_text: production company takes perpetual master ownership plus a large cut of any future label deal, with no time limit on the exclusivity.
risk_2_text: vague 'reasonable efforts' shopping obligation with no deadline — artist can be locked up indefinitely with no deal materializing.

title: Songwriter Collaboration Agreement
money_fields: Ownership percentage per writer | Who administers/collects (self, publisher, PRO) and how collected money is distributed
rights_grant_notes: Confirms this only covers the composition/publishing, not any master recording made of it
control_fields: Approval rights for licensing the song (samples, sync, cover versions) — unanimous or majority? | What happens if one writer wants to license the song and another objects
intake_questions: What are the agreed percentage splits between writers? | Should any single writer be able to approve licenses on their own for their share, or does everyone need to agree? | Is a formal split sheet also needed for PRO registration? (recommend yes)
risk_1_text: no default rule for what happens if writers can't agree on a license request — can freeze the song indefinitely.
risk_2_text: simple percentage splits with each writer independently able to license their own share (standard and artist-friendly) if that's the intent — confirm it's actually wanted.

title: Songwriter Split Sheet (Detailed / PRO-Registration)
money_fields: No payment terms — this document captures PRO-registration data alongside ownership percentages.
rights_grant_notes: Splits the composition/publishing and captures lyrics-vs-music percentage breakdown per writer. | Captures PRO affiliation (ASCAP/BMI/SESAC) and CAE/IPI number for royalty routing.
control_fields: Sample disclosure required. | SSN field in the source template should generally be omitted or collected through a separate secure channel.
intake_questions: Song title, session date(s), recording artist, and label? | For each writer: legal name, publishing company (if any), PRO affiliation, and lyrics/music percentage split? | Does any writer already have a publisher entitled to a percentage?
risk_1_text: Total ownership percentages across all writers do not sum to 100%.
risk_2_text: A writer's publishing percentage is not clarified as carved-out-of vs. in-addition-to their writer's share.
risk_3_text: Privacy flag: full Social Security Numbers should not be embedded in a document that will be widely shared; recommend collecting tax ID separately.

title: Split Sheet
money_fields: No payment terms — this document only allocates ownership percentages.
rights_grant_notes: Splits the composition/publishing only, not the master recording. | Percentages across all writers must total exactly 100%.
control_fields: Sample/interpolation disclosure required before finalizing. | Each writer must sign; no partial execution.
intake_questions: Song title and session date? | Full legal names and percentage for every contributor? | Does the composition contain any sample, interpolation, or replay?
risk_1_text: Percentages do not sum to 100% — verify math before finalizing.
risk_2_text: A beatmaker paid under a separate license is listed as a co-writer without confirming the license grants a composition percentage.
risk_3_text: Prompt splits documentation right after a session is the single best low-cost habit for avoiding future disputes.

title: Studio Time Agreement
money_fields: Hourly or block rate, deposit, and payment due timing | Overtime rate if sessions run long
rights_grant_notes: Confirms the client (artist) owns the resulting masters unless the studio explicitly retains any interest (e.g., in-house engineer/producer taking points)
control_fields: Cancellation/no-show/late policy and any fees | File delivery format and timeline after the session | Studio's right to use session as demo reel/portfolio (should require artist consent)
intake_questions: How many hours/sessions are booked, and at what rate? | Is an engineer/producer included, and do they expect any royalty interest beyond the hourly rate? | What's the cancellation/no-show policy? | How and when will final files be delivered?
risk_1_text: studio claims any ownership interest in the recordings by default — should be an explicit, separate negotiation (see Producer Royalties Agreement), not baked into a simple rental.
risk_2_text: clear cancellation policy protects both sides.

title: Sync / Master Use License Agreement
money_fields: Sync fee (flat, one-time is typical) and whether it covers both master and publishing or just one | Back-end royalties (if the project generates ongoing revenue, e.g., a TV show in syndication)
rights_grant_notes: Exact scope: which project, which cut/edit, what media (TV, streaming, social, ads), what territory, and for how long (perpetuity vs. defined term) | Most-favored-nations clause if multiple rights holders are involved (all get equal terms)
control_fields: Approval rights over how the music is used (contextual approval — e.g., not paired with content the artist finds objectionable) | Credit requirements
intake_questions: What specific project, episode/scene, or campaign is this for? | What media and territory does the licensee need (broadcast, streaming, social, paid ads, worldwide vs. one country)? | Is this a flat fee, or does the artist want a share of backend revenue (e.g., ad revenue on a viral campaign)? | Does the artist have any restrictions on context (e.g., not political ads, not competitor brands)?
risk_1_text: 'in perpetuity, throughout the universe, all media' grant for a flat one-time fee with no cap on how the music can be reused later (sequels, spin-offs, ads).
risk_2_text: no most-favored-nations clause when both the master and publishing sides need separate approval — one side could undercut the other's rate.

title: Talent / Likeness Release Form
money_fields: Flat fee, if any, or confirmation this is unpaid/for exposure (flag if unpaid and commercial use is broad)
rights_grant_notes: Scope of use — specific project only, or broad/perpetual/all-media use. Perpetual releases for no or minimal pay are a common artist-risk pattern and should be flagged.
control_fields: Whether the talent can revoke consent, and any context restrictions (e.g., not for political or competing-brand use)
intake_questions: What specific project/use is this release for? | Is there compensation, and is it a flat fee or ongoing? | Should the release be limited to this project, or does the user intend broader use?
risk_1_text: perpetual, worldwide, all-media likeness release for free or a small flat fee with no context restriction.
risk_2_text: no expiration or defined project scope — release could be reused for unrelated future projects.

title: Talent / Producer Agreement
money_fields: Fee structure and payment schedule | Whether any royalty/backend applies
rights_grant_notes: Confirms whether this is work-for-hire (producer/company owns the result) or the talent retains rights
control_fields: Deliverables, deadlines, and revision rounds | Credit
intake_questions: What exactly is the talent being engaged to do, and what's the deliverable? | Is this work-for-hire, or does the talent keep any rights/royalty in the result? | What's the fee and payment schedule?
risk_1_text: ownership of the resulting work not clearly stated — always define this explicitly.

title: Venue Performance Agreement
money_fields: Fee structure (flat, door split, or bar minimum) | Deposit and cancellation/refund policy
rights_grant_notes: Confirms performance service only — no transfer of recording or composition rights unless a separate recording clause is added
control_fields: Load-in/soundcheck/performance times | Who provides sound/lighting equipment and staff | Liability and insurance responsibility for equipment and injury
intake_questions: What's the date, load-in/set times, and total fee structure? | Who's providing sound and lighting — the venue or the artist? | What's the cancellation policy for weather, illness, or low ticket sales?
risk_1_text: no clear liability/insurance allocation — artist could be on the hook for venue equipment damage or injury claims.
risk_2_text: vague cancellation terms with no defined refund of deposit.

title: Venue Rental Contract
money_fields: Rental fee, deposit, and payment schedule | Additional costs (security, cleaning, overtime hours)
rights_grant_notes: Confirms a space-rental relationship — not a co-promotion or revenue-share deal unless explicitly added
control_fields: Set-up/breakdown windows, capacity limits, and permitted activities (alcohol, filming, ticketing) | Insurance requirements (event insurance, certificate of insurance naming the venue) | Damage deposit refund conditions
intake_questions: What are the exact dates/times needed, including setup and breakdown? | What's the rental fee, deposit, and what does the deposit cover/how is it refunded? | Does the renter need to provide a certificate of insurance? | What activities need to be explicitly permitted (alcohol service, filming, ticket sales)?
risk_1_text: no cap on additional/overtime fees — can balloon the cost after the event.
risk_2_text: insurance requirement not specified — confirm what coverage and limits the venue requires before signing.

title: Videographer / Photographer Release
money_fields: Flat fee, if any, for the shoot
rights_grant_notes: Who owns the resulting images/footage — typically the photographer/videographer owns the copyright while granting the subject a license to use it personally/promotionally | Whether the creator can license the images to third parties (stock, press) or only use for portfolio
control_fields: Can the subject request approval before public use of specific images? | Credit requirements for the photographer/videographer
intake_questions: What's the shoot for (music video, promo photos, behind-the-scenes)? | Does the artist need approval rights before images/footage are used publicly? | Can the photographer/videographer license these to others, or is use limited to this project and the artist's own promo?
risk_1_text: no license-back to the subject — artist should always retain the right to use their own photos/video for promo.
risk_2_text: creator granted rights to sell/license images to third parties without artist approval, when that wasn't the intent.

title: Work-for-Hire Agreement
money_fields: Flat fee (work-for-hire is almost always a one-time buyout, not royalty-bearing) | Payment schedule tied to delivery/milestones
rights_grant_notes: Confirms complete transfer of copyright to the hiring party — the contractor keeps nothing unless a royalty/credit is separately negotiated | This is the highest-risk-of-regret template for the contractor — make sure they understand it's a full buyout before they sign as the one giving up rights
control_fields: Delivery deadline and format | Revision rounds included | Credit, if any (work-for-hire doesn't guarantee credit unless stated)
intake_questions: Which side is the user on — the hiring party or the person being hired? | What's being created, and what's the flat fee? | Does the contractor want any credit, even though this is a full buyout? | Is the contractor fully aware this gives up all future royalty/ownership interest? (if unsure, flag for attorney review before finalizing)
risk_1_text: when a substantial or potentially high-value work is being fully bought out for a flat fee — make sure the contractor actually intends to give up all future royalty/backend interest.
risk_2_text: no credit provision even though the contractor expected one — add explicit credit language if desired.
